In 1996 California deregulated its electricity industry and required\\nthe State\\'s privately owned utility companies to divest themselves of their\\ngenerating plants.  The purpose of deregulation was to introduce competition\\ninto the electricity markets, with the intention of reducing rates for\\nelectrical power.  In fact, however, certain participants in this recently\\nderegulated industry have, in violation of their operating Tariff, taken\\nadvantage of structural flaws in the system and improperly obtained\\nconfidential competitor information to artificially inflate prices for\\nelectricity, yielding themselves billions of dollars in windfall profits at\\nthe expense of California consumers.\\n22. As part of the deregulation, several new entities were created to\\nfacilitate the workings of this new market.  California\\'s investor owned\\nutilities, Pacific Gas & Electric (PG&E), Southern California Edison (SCE),\\nand San Diego Gas & Electric (SDG&E) (the\"Utilities\"), now purchase\\nelectricity for their customers from independent generators and traders,\\nincluding defendants, through a market known as the California Power\\nExchange (PX).  The PX maintains a market for the purchase and sale of\\nwholesale electricity through a variety of forward contracts and real time\\nmarkets.  Under the California deregulatory scheme, the Utilities were,\\nuntil just recently, required to purchase power through the PX and\\nprohibited from independently contracting for power outside this market.\\n23. The deregulated market also led to the creation of the California\\nIndependent System Operator (CAISO).  The CAISO is an \"independent\"\\nnon-profit corporation, though its managing board includes representatives\\nfrom among the generators and traders, that was created to manage the flow\\nof electricity and ensure reliability along the long distance, high-voltage\\npower lines that make up the bulk of California\\'s transmission system.\\nApproximately 75% of California\\'s electricity is distributed through the\\nCAISO managed  \"power grid\".  The CAISO monitors electrical loads (i.e.,\\ndemand) on an on-going basis and ensures that there is an adequate supply of\\npower to meet that demand.\\n/ / /\\n 24. The CAISO accomplishes this by maintaining a Real Time Imbalance\\nMarket (the \"Real Time Market\").  When the CAISO receives bids from\\nsuppliers that are insufficient to meet the demand for power, it must accept\\nany bid, which then sets the market-clearing price for that hour. Under the\\nsingle price auction system used by the CAISO, all sellers of electricity in\\nthe Real Time Market automatically receive the market clearing price, which\\nis the (second) highest price paid in the market, even if they were willing\\nto sell and had in fact bid to sell electricity at lower prices. This\\nmechanism allows sophisticated market participants, such as defendants, to\\ngame the market by withholding bids in an effort to maximize the clearing\\nprice.\\n25. The Real Time Market was not designed to handle large transactions,\\nbut merely to provide a mechanism to correct short term imbalances in supply\\nand demand.  Defendants nonetheless pushed a substantial portion of the\\ndaily wholesale electricity sales into this market by under bidding capacity\\nto the forward market leaving wholesale customers no alternative place to\\nobtain the power to satisfy their retail customers\\' demand.\\n26. The CAISO also manages the Replacement Reserve Market, which is used\\nto balance supply and demand of electricity.  Sellers in the Replacement\\nReserve Market receive a fixed premium for having available capacity.  If\\ncalled upon by the ISO to deliver energy, sellers in the Replacement Reserve\\nMarket also receive the Real Time Market price.  Thus, if generators know\\nthat capacity is short, they have an incentive to withhold supplies from the\\nspot markets and push as much as possible into the Replacement Reserve\\nMarket.  Access to real time generating information facilitates such\\n\"gaming\" of the markets by demonstrating, in real time, available competing\\nsupply.\\n27. In times of high demand, the CAISO has the authority to purchase\\nenergy from out-of-state sources, as to which there is no operative price\\ncap.  The CAISO was forced to do so during the Summer of 2000.  California\\ngenerators and marketers can export electricity to surrounding markets in\\norder to create artificial shortages and drive up prices in the California\\nmarkets.  They can then resell that electricity to the CAISO at inflated and\\nuncapped prices.  As the PX Compliance Committee noted in its November 1,\\n2000 Report (\"the PX Compliance Report\"):\\n/ / /\\n \"During periods of high Out-of-Market purchases, when prices are above the\\nReal-Time energy price cap, in-state generators have an incentive to export\\nenergy out of California. Evidence of such behavior may be derived from\\na number of circumstances, including:\\n\\nMMIP 2.1.1.1  withholding of generation capacity under circumstances in\\nwhich it would normally be offered in a competitive market;\\n\\nMMIP 2.1.1.2  unexplained or unusual redeclarations of availability by\\nGenerators;\\n\\nMMIP 2.1.1.3  unusual trades or transactions;\\n\\nMMIP 2.1.1.4  pricing and bidding patterns that are inconsistent with\\nprevailing supply and demand conditions, e.g., prices and bids that appear\\nconsistently excessive for or otherwise inconsistent with such conditions;\\nand\\n\\nMMIP 2.1.1.5  unusual activity or circumstances relating to imports from or\\nexports to other markets or exchanges.\\n\\nThe Market Surveillance Unit shall evaluate, on an ongoing basis, whether\\nthe continued or persistent presence of such circumstances indicates the\\npresence of behavior that is designed to or has the potential to distort the\\noperation and efficient functioning of a competitive market, e.g., the\\nstrategic withholding and redeclaring of capacity, and whether it indicates\\nthe presence and exercise of market power or of other unacceptable\\npractices.\\n\\n37. MMIP Section 2.1.3 states in relevant part:\\n\\n\"Gaming\", or taking unfair advantage of the rules and procedures set forth\\nin the PX or ISO Tariffs, Protocols or Activity Rules, or of transmission\\nconstraints in periods in which exist substantial Congestion, to the\\ndetriment of the efficiency of, and of consumers in, the ISO Markets.\\n\"Gaming\" may also include taking undue advantage of other conditions that\\nmay affect the availability of transmission and generation capacity, such as\\nloop flow, facility outages, level of hydropower output or seasonal limits\\non energy imports from out-of-state, or actions or behaviors that may\\notherwise render the system and the ISO markets vulnerable to price\\nmanipulation to the detriment of their efficiency.\\n\\n 38. Market participants used their trade organization, the WSCC, to\\nshare access to and use real time information, notwithstanding the fact that\\nits publication and use violated the  ISO\\'s operating procedures, as set\\nforth in tariffs and protocols that were filed with and approved by FERC,\\nand by adoption made part of the contracts by  which defendants were\\nauthorized to sell electricity to the PX.  Those tariffs and protocols\\nrequired that such data be kept confidential to prevent gaming the market\\nand not be used by market participants to engage in anti-competitive\\nbehavior.\\n39. It has been reported in the Dow Jones Work. Com Newswire on October\\n19, 2000, that:\\n\"Electricity generators may have used real-time plant activity reports from\\nthe state\\'s grid operator to their advantage in California\\'s wholesale\\nelectricity market, according to an official with the Western Systems\\nCoordinating Council.\\n\\n * * * * * * *\\n\\n\"At issue is real-time information the California Independent System\\nOperator provided the Western systems Coordinating Council, a governmental\\n[sic] organization that monitors electricity reliability in the western\\nU.S., about power plant activity in the state.\\n\\n\"The real-time information allows market participants . . . to access data\\nvia an internet site that shows how much capacity a plant with more than 200\\nmegawatts has online at any given moment. . . . .\\n\\n\"The information was intended to be used to monitor electric reliability on\\nthe grid . . . .\\n\\n\"Last month, however, the ISO\\'s attorneys alerted the WSCC that the \\'data is\\nbeing used against them and to game the market,\\' according to Bill Commish,\\ndirector of dispatch with the WSCC.\\n\\n * * * * * *\\n\\n\"Commish said generators could use the information to withhold supply and\\ndrive up power prices or to identify transmission congestion in a particular\\nregion and use that to gouge customers.\\n\\n\"However, the ISO, which controls about 75% of the state\\'s power grid and\\nreal-time market, may have violated a FERC rule because it is required to\\nkeep such information confidential for 90 days, an ISO attorney told the\\nWSCC.\\n\\n\"Beginning Monday, the ISO will no longer provide such information  to the\\nWSCC or other market participants.\"\\n\\n 40. Starting on or about May 22, 2000, Defendants used such real time\\ndata to exercise market power by, among other things, reducing their output,\\nstrategically under-bidding supply to the forward markets, and exporting\\nelectricity from the State in order to drive up the Real Time Market price\\nand other market prices.  As a direct result of their improper access to and\\nuse of this information, the price of wholesale electricity spiked sharply\\nupwards on May 22, 2000 and has remained at artificially inflated prices\\never since.  FERC, CPUC, and CAISO Dept. of Market Analysis, have all now\\nconcluded that market participants should be excluded from the CAISO board.\\n41. As noted in the North County Times on October 19, 2000:\\n\"A case study of San Diego County\\'s two big power plants has concluded that\\nthey held back from full production of electricity in June, even as prices\\nskyrocketed and California\\'s power manager was scrambling for supplies to\\nprevent blackouts.\\n\\n\"To the study\\'s author . . . the low production in San Diego county is clear\\nevidence that the companies that generate and trade electricity in CA were\\ncreating an artificial shortage to drive up prices.\\n\\n * * * * * *\\n\\nMcCullough\\'s hour-by-hour analysis of power output for June found that the\\nEncina plant in Carlsbad generated 44 percent of the megawatt hours that it\\ncould have during periods when prices were higher than the plant\\'s cost of\\nproduction.  The South Bay power plant in Chula Vista generated 61 percent\\nof what would be expected under traditional economic theory.\\n\\nEconomists estimate it costs $45-$55 per megawatt hour to generate\\nelectricity at the plants. The wholesale price in June averaged $120 per\\nmegawatt hour.\\n\\nA separate analysis conducted by the North County Times revealed \"mysterious\\ncutbacks in Carlsbad during a heady market of sky-high prices.\"\\n\\n * * ** *\\n\\n\"Investigators and market analysts have documented extensive evidence that\\nelectricity traders have waited until prices rose on California\\'s market\\nthis summer before they would commit their power plants to production.\"\\n\\n\"\\'We did see evidence of withholding in the bidding,\\' according to Jim\\nDetmers, the ISO\\'s operations chief.\"\\n\\n 42. In addition, defendants used such real time information about their\\ncompetitors to improperly withhold electrical supplies from the forward\\nmarkets operated by the PX in order to take advantage of the ISO\\'s need to\\nbalance supply and demand in the spot market and thereby benefit from the\\nsingle price auction system by obtaining the highest price paid at any given\\nperiod.  In addition, certain defendants sold or parked electricity with\\naffiliates in other states in order to artificially drive up prices in the\\nCalifornia markets.  They then sold that electricity back into the\\nCalifornia markets at the artificially inflated prices they had created.\\nThese tactics forced buyers in the California wholesale electricity market\\nto purchase more than 30% of their electricity needs in the inflated Spot\\nMarket, rather than the less than 5% that should be sold in that market. The\\nSpot Market was solely intended to satisfy last minute fluctuations in the\\ndemand for energy.\\nC. Results of Defendants\\' Activities\\n43. From late May 2000 through the present, defendants\\' activities have\\nraised wholesale electricity prices to record levels, well above the rates\\nthat would prevail in a competitive marketplace and disproportionate to the\\ncosts of generating that electricity.  Those prices have resulted in an\\napproximate tripling of electricity rates in areas served by SDG&E, where\\nretail rates have been deregulated and represent in large part a pass\\nthrough of SDG&E\\'s costs for such power, which it purchases from the\\ndefendant generators and traders through the California Power Exchange.\\n44. As the Market Surveillance Committee (\"MSC\") of the CAISO concluded\\nin its September 6, 2000 Report (\"the MSC Report\"), during the months of May\\nand June 2000 revenues from the sale of ISO loads in the California energy\\nmarket were 37% and 182%, respectively, above the revenues that would have\\nbeen generated under competitive pricing conditions.    MSC Report at p. 2.\\nThe MSC Report unambiguously concluded that market participants exercised a\\n\"significant amount of  market power\" in the California energy markets,\\nbeginning as early as October 1999 and increasing dramatically during the\\nClass Period.  Id. at pp. 4, 15, 17.\\n45. The average market clearing price in California\\'s wholesale markets\\nduring August of 2000 was $166.24/MWh under moderate load conditions,\\ncompared with $32.31/MWh a year earlier.  While load demand conditions in\\nCalifornia during August 2000 were slightly higher than in August 1999, they\\nwere similar to those during August 1998 when prices were much lower.  Peak\\ndemand in August 2000 was lower than in August of either of the prior two\\nyears, negating representations by industry leaders that excessive demand\\ncaused these price increases.  Indeed, some California electricity producers\\nwere only running at 60% of capacity during the so-called emergency periods.\\n\\n 46. These price hikes have even been effect during the middle of the\\nnight, when electricity is abundant and demand is low.  Further, prices in\\nNovember 2000, when demand for electricity is much lower than during the\\nsummer months, continue to be substantially in excess of the prior years\\'\\nlevels and in excess of the levels that should prevail in a competitive\\nmarketplace.\\n47. As a result of defendants\\' exercise of market power, they\\nartificially increased prices to record levels and have obtained huge\\nwindfall profits.  As reported in the October 17, 2000 San Diego Union\\nTribune,  analyst Anatol Feygin of JP Morgan estimated that electricity\\nindustry profits from California for the 3 months ended September 30, 2000\\ncould reach $6 billion, even after taking into account cost increases.\\nFeygin stated, \"\\'The industry was literally at eight times the profitability\\nof last year . . .. that is a fortune.\\'\"\\n48. People are literally dying financially from\\nthis situation.\"  Work.com Newswire (10/21/00).\\n52. The improper sharing and use of real time wholesale electricity\\ngeneration and transmission data by defendants to withhold generation by\\nunplanned outages and to maintain bidding strategies which led to contrived\\nand artificial shortages, and other manipulative conduct, had the effect of\\nartificially inflating and maintaining wholesale electricity prices above\\ncompetitive prices allowing defendants to reap illegal profits amounting to\\nbillions of dollars, at the expense of plaintiffs and the class.\\n FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION\\n Violation of Sections 16720 and 16726\\n of the California Business and Professions Code\\n Trust In Restraint of Trade or Commerce in Violation of the\\nAntitrust Act\\n (Against All Defendants)\\n\\n53. Plaintiffs reallege and incorporate by reference each and every\\nallegation set forth above.\\n54. The Cartwright Act states, at o16726, that: \"Except as provided in\\nthis chapter, every trust is unlawful, against public policy and void.\"  A\\ntrust is defined at o16720 as follows:\\n55. \"A trust is a combination of capital, skill or acts by two or more\\npersons for any of the following purposes:\\n(a) To create or carry out restrictions in trade or commerce.\\n\\n(b) To limit or reduce the production, or increase the price of\\nmerchandise or of any commodity.\\n\\n(c) To prevent competition in manufacturing, making, transportation,\\nsale or purchase of merchandise, produce or any commodity.\\n\\n(d) To fix at any standard or figure, whereby its price to the public or\\nconsumer shall be in any manner controlled or established, any article or\\ncommodity of merchandise, produce or commerce intended for sale, barter, use\\nor consumption in this State.\\n\\n(e) To make or enter into or execute or carry out any contracts,\\nobligations, or agreements of any kind or description, by which they do all\\nor any or any combination of the following:\\n\\n (1) Bind themselves not to sell, dispose of or transport any article or\\nany commodity or any article of trade, use, merchandise, commerce or\\nconsumption below a common standard figure, or fixed value.\\n\\n(2) Agree in any manner to keep the price of such article, commodity or\\ntransportation at a fixed or graduated figure.\\n\\n(3) Establish or settle the price of any article, commodity or\\ntransportation between them or themselves and others, so as directly or\\nindirectly to preclude a free and unrestricted competition among themselves,\\nor any purchasers or consumers in the sale or transportation of any such\\narticle or commodity.\\n\\n(4) Agree to pool, combine or directly or indirectly unite any interests\\nthat they may have connected with the sale or transportation of any such\\narticle or commodity, that its price might in any manner be affected.\"\\n\\n56. The\\nCartwright Act states:\\nAny person who is injured in his or her business or property by reason of\\nanything forbidden or declared unlawful by this chapter, may sue therefore\\n. . . and to recover three times the damages sustained by him or her,\\ninterest . . . and preliminary or permanent injunctive relief . . . .\\n\\n57. Plaintiffs reallege and incorporate by reference each and every\\nallegation set forth above.\\n68. As alleged hereinabove, beginning as early as May, 2000, defendants\\nunlawfully conspired, agreed, arranged and combined to prevent and restrain\\ncompetition for the sale of electricity, in violation of oo 16700 et seq.\\nand oo 17200 et seq. of the B&P Code.\\n70. Plaintiff and the Class have no adequate remedy at law for their\\nirreparable injuries.\\n73. Defendants\\' acts, contracts, agreements, conspiracies, and\\ncombinations in restraint of trade and free and open competition, alleged\\nherein, violate the Antitrust Act. Section 17200 et seq. of the California Business & Professions Code\\nprohibits acts of unfair competition, which include any \"unlawful, unfair,\\nor fraudulent business act or practice and unfair, deceptive, untrue or\\nmisleading advertising\".\\n76. Defendants charged rates for wholesale electricity that were\\nunconscionable given their cost of production, the newly emergent markets\\nfor that product, and the consumers\\' need for electrical power.\\n87. Defendants\\' rates were  inherently  excessive, invalid and\\nunconscionable, particularly in light of the deceptive and manipulative\\npractices they used to inflate the market prices and the vital need\\nconsumers and businesses have for electrical power.\\n/ / /\\n 88. Can you forward the complaint (suit) as an\\nattachment?\\n\\nMark\\n'}]"}
summary: Defendants in the email thread include Reliant and Dynegy, who reported significant increases in earnings. The email mentions the high cost of producing electricity in San Diego County and how defendants' conduct caused a tripling of SDG&E customers' bills. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) concluded that wholesale prices in California were "unjust and unreasonable" due to market power exercised by generators and traders. The plaintiffs allege violations of the California Business and Professions Code, the Unfair Trade Practices Act, the Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and unconscionability. They seek damages, injunctive relief, and other remedies. Mark requests the complaint (suit) as an attachment.

The email thread discusses scheduling a half-day offsite for Enron North America Corp. The options are Wednesday, May 23 or Thursday, May 24. Carol St. Clair initially suggests both dates and asks for preferences. Brent Hendry mentions a conflict with a legal/credit seminar on Wednesday, so Thursday would be better for him. Cheryl Nelson expresses a preference for Wednesday. Overall, the majority seems to lean towards Thursday, but no final decision is made.

summary: The Gas Fundamentals Website has been updated with added security. Users are now required to login with their Windows Domain name and password. If users do not want to be prompted with this information again, they can check the "Save this password in your password list" option. Amanda Huble forwards this information to various groups within the company. David Dronet provides the initial update and instructions for accessing the website.

The City League has revised the flag football schedule once again. The team will be playing the Jay Ballers three times during the season and the Raiders only once. The sender is unsure why this is the case, but believes it will work to their advantage as the Raiders are a stronger team. All games will be held on Wednesday nights at Jaycee Park ballfield. Directions to the park are provided.

Jim wants to schedule a conference call for Wednesday afternoon. Michael suggests contacting Exelon, Constellation, Edison Mission Energy, Reliant, Duke, Mirant, PG&E, and Cinergy. He recommends NG make contact with the executives instead of Enron to hedge their position. Jim agrees and asks for phone numbers. He also mentions that NG is willing to do a conference call on Wednesday or a meeting on Thursday.

Jeff confirms his availability for a meeting and provides his office number. Jim mentions that he has no further additions and assumes Dave understands the link between rate freeze end and payment. Vicki forwards a memo from Bob and asks for comments. Jeff replies with his comments. The email thread revolves around reviewing and providing feedback on a negative CTC memo for Delainey.

Greg suggests scheduling a meeting for Tuesday at 11:45. Phillip proposes either next Tuesday or Thursday. Shirley asks Vince if the meeting is an interview or a business meeting. Vince asks Shirley to call and discuss the best timing for a visit from Ehud Ronn. Shijie Deng expresses interest in visiting Vince's research group in late July or early August. Vince responds and says his assistant will call to discuss the timing. A separate email thread includes Carol St. Clair forwarding EnronOnline documents to Tana Jones at the request of Carol St. Clair.

Megan informs Daren that TXU has revised their rates for January 2001. The rates for contract 1671 are now $0.10 and $0.08, instead of the previous $0.10. She asks Daren to change the demand fee on deal 384258 accordingly. Megan also discusses the rate discrepancy on contract 1856 and mentions the El Paso header fee. She provides the correct rate for contract 1856 and leaves a copy of the contract for Daren. Daren acknowledges the changes and mentions adjusting the spreadsheet based on their previous conversation. Megan also mentions other updates regarding Apache and the Tenaska meters.

Tracy and Julie are discussing the scheduling of a meeting for the NNG/TW Actual project. Tracy suggests Thursday morning, but Julie mentions that Danny is available from 8:30 to 11:00. Tracy mentions that she has a conflicting staff meeting with Rod but can miss it if necessary. Julie also mentions that she has Friday morning open. Danny is asked to consider the material to be covered in the meeting, and Julie will set up a meeting for him and Tracy to discuss it further.

Mark Pickering, the Chief Technology Officer at Enron Net Works, expresses dissatisfaction with the HR assistance provided. David Oxley responds, stating that he and Robert have a plan and that Mark's team will change next week. Mark expresses his disappointment again and mentions that he doesn't want any employees from the HR department. Another email from Chris Germany asks who the HR representative is.

Kathy Reeves noticed that the P&L reported for Canada in the management reports for 2000 was incorrect. She believes the problem stems from a Q1 origination adjustment that was not included in the reports. Robin Rodrigue, however, states that the 2000 DPR is closed and no more changes can be made. He suggests that either the adjustment was never made or it is already included in their reported numbers. Kathy expresses her concern that the P&L in Robin's report is $4.1M too high and that the breakout by trader is not accurate.

Laine is waiting for a response regarding the Escrow Agreement and plans to call if necessary. Vince wants the software to be in the London office for use in negotiations with European clients. Stinson suggests a 2-day response time for software support and a payment schedule that incentivizes early release. Karla asks about Enron's plans for the source code and if they intend to reverse engineer or use it to create their own product. Vince mentions using workstations in London and Houston. Karla points out missing pricing information in the proposal and asks if more details are needed.

Mark Palmer informs Barney about six equity analysts, three from the buy side and three from the sell side, who recommend Enron stock. He mentions that all three buy side analysts are increasing their holdings in Enron shares. Melissa Prihoda asks Errol and Phillip to schedule a meeting to discuss the Utility Track for two new analysts joining their group. Jana expresses her interest in having an analyst start as soon as possible and asks for the procedure. She also mentions that the gas trading desk director, Phillip Allen, supports the idea of analysts rotating into her group. Lastly, someone is in need of two analysts for a period of 2-6 months for commercial business analysis roles related to EOTT.

Richardson Energy Marketing, Ltd. is seeking a master netting agreement. Nidia Mendoza in Credit is gathering information on their trading activities with Enron. Richardson Energy Marketing, Ltd. trades physical natural gas liquids with Enron Gas Liquids, physical natural gas with Enron North America Corp., and financial natural gas through an ISDA Master agreement with Enron North America Corp. Marie is assigned to handle the agreement and will receive a list of counterparties from Nidia.

The email thread discusses a proposed draft exhibit that goes beyond the ALJ's order. The exhibit should be narrowly focused on the mismatch of capacity, but it includes inaccurate and misleading information. The column titled "Total Take-away Capacity" and the "Avg. Daily Market" box should be eliminated. The group is not satisfied with the exhibit and suggests that the person responsible for it file their own exhibit.

Robin Barbe is requesting the origination of two deals from TP1. Robin Rodrigue forwards an email to his team, informing them of the new origination report that will be given to Fred Lagrasta each morning. The report will be based on the Origination schedule tab of their P&L file and will require additional information for Middle Market Nymex Originations. Michael Benien provides a list of book admins for different categories. Susan asks Agustin for the correct origination amount before booking a deal with General de Cermica.

{"subject": "RE: Enfolio Master Firm Purchase/Sale Agreement", "messages": "[{'timestamp': datetime.datetime(2001, 3, 8, 9, 13), 'from': 'Dan J Hyvl', 'to': array(['"Kolling', 'Grant" <grant_kolling@city.palo-alto.ca.us>@ENRON'],
       dtype=object), 'body': 'Grant,\n I have reviewed your requested changes and have made the changes which do \nnot require explanation or clarification.  Those changes are reflected in the \nabove document.  Let me go over your list of items:\n 1. I have deleted the word "DRAFT".\n 2. I have left a blank for the date within the month of March 2001 when the \ncontract would be executed by the City.\n 3. I have changed the word "may" to "shall".\n 4. Maximum Daily Delivery Point Quantity does not fit in a Deficiency \nDefault, it is just the maximum quantity that can be handled by a party at a \nparticular point.  I do not think their is an omission.\n 5. I have added the word "reasonable".\n 6. The procedue for how the Termination Payment is determined is provided, \nif the City disagrees with the method and values provided in the statement \nand is unable to convince the Company to revise, the statement, then the \nissue is to be resolved in arbitration.  At the point that a Termination \nPayment calculation is necessary, a long drawn out period should not be \nnecessary to attain closure.\n 7. We need to limit the duration to 30 days,  neither party should be \nrequired to wait 60 days before it could accelerate the other party\'s \nobligations under the Contract.  We might be able to add language to extend \nthe period if we had some documentation stating the steps that a party was \npursuing to cause the proceeding to be dismissed and the other party was \notherwise kept whole from a credit exposure.\n 8. I have kept the 30 days because 5 days is too short a period.  During a \nholiday period, one scheduling error could cover the entire period.  Article \n3 has language which provides a remedy for a party if a scheduling default \nextends for more than 5 days during any month. \n 9. The reason is because Enron Corp. is the rated entity and no separate \nrating applies to ENA.\n 10. I have changed "a" to "the"\n 11. I have eliminated the  60 day limitation on the duration of an event of \nForce Majeure.\n 12. This merely addressed the possibility of a imbalance amount being due \nwhen a pipeline aggregates imbalances using multiple points, and the language \nwould allocated the payment based on the amount of the imbalance that a \nparticular party may have caused.  I think the language is clear as written.\n 13. The definition of Act was one of the items that I had requested that you \nreview and complete as necessary so that all appropriate statutes were \nreferenced.  I am still waiting for your language.  I started filling it in \nusing language that had been provided by the City.\n 14. I added the word "reasonable".\n 15. I have made the requested change relating to GAAAP.\n 16. This is a late payment provision and as such a believe that the \nprovision should be more than a party\'s rating, as such I have kept the 2% \nover prime language.\n 17. These amounts were determined by the credit group and any change needs \nto be discussed with that group.  BBB-  is considered investment grade and I \nunderstand that Enron Corp.\'s rating is BBB.  ENA is not a rated entity and \nthat is why the language relates to Enron Corp.\'s rating.\n 18. The elimination of the opinion of counsel did not change the \nrequirements relating to the representations that we expect the City to have \nmade.  If the City cannot make these representations, then we need to know \nthat before we execute the Contract.\n 19. I have added the word "reasonable".\n 20. The party that has the Transport Agreement with the Transporter should \nhave the legal right to obtain the information based on its contract.  \n 21. It is our position that any dispute be arbitrated.  We can agree to \nmeditation if we can make the outcome binding on the parties.  I am willing \nto discuss any changed language that you might care to offer.\n 22. We have found that personnel of both our Company and that of our \nCustomers change so rapidily that the list is not workable and merely allows \na party to back out of transactions it does not like on the basis that the \nperson who agreed to such transaction was not on the list.  Therefore , we \nobject to any listing of approved parties who can transact.  We believe that \neach party should be responsible for the actions of its employees and should \nstand behind any transactions that those parties may enter into pursuant to \nthe terms and provisions of the Contract.  \n\n I will be out of the office on Friday, but will be in all next week if you \ncare to discuss any of these matters.\n\n\n\n\t"Kolling, Grant" <grant_kolling@city.palo-alto.ca.us>\n\t03/02/2001 03:43 PM\n\t\t \n\t\t To: "\'Dan.J.Hyvl@enron.com\'" <Dan.J.Hyvl@enron.com>, "Kolling, Grant" \n<grant_kolling@city.palo-alto.ca.us>\n\t\t cc: Kim.Ward@enron.com\n\t\t Subject: RE: Enfolio Master Firm Purchase/Sale Agreement\n\n\n <<0071988 RESO Enron.doc>>\n\nDan:\n\nFirst, I\'ve attached the proposed resolution which authorizes the City\nManager to execute the Enfolio agreement.\n\nMore importantly, I need to inform you that our senior management has\nreviewed the referenced contract; I have been asked to present additional\nchanges to the agreement for Enron\'s consideration and to raise questions\nabout certain of its terms and conditions.\n\nLet me start from page 1, top to bottom, and proceed to the end of the\nexhibits.\n\n1.  There is the word "DRAFT" above the title of the Enfolio agreement which\nshould be deleted.\n\n2.  The introductory paragraph, line 5, should not contain the words "1st of\nJanuary, 2001."  It should be left blank, until the parties have signed the\ncontract.  Otherwise, the City will be in breach as of the date it signs the\ncontract, because Article 2, section 2.1 requires the City to proffer the\nto-be-approved-by-Council resolution as of 1/1/01.\n\n3.  Article 2, Section 2.4, line 2.  The City (Customer) wants Enron\n(Company) to confirm every recorded telephonic Transaction, as defined.\nTherefore, the City requests the word "may" should be changed to "shall."\n\n4.  Article 3, Sections 3.1 and 3.2, first sentence:   Buyer\'s Requested\nQuantity refers to the DCQ or MaxDQ.  Seller\'s failure to Schedule the\nBuyer\'s Requested Quantity shall constitute a Seller\'s Deficiency Default.\nHow does a Maximum Daily Delivery Point Quantity fit into a Seller\'s\nDeficiency Default if the Buyer\'s Requested Quantity does not include a\nMaximum Daily Delivery Point Quantity?  What is the reason for the omission?\n\n5.  Article 4, Section 4.1, lines 15 and 23:  Line 23 refers to "reasonable\nattorneys\' fees" yet line 15 refers to "attorneys\' fees."  To be internally\nconsistent, line 15 should say "reasonable attorneys\' fees."\n\n6.  Section 4.1, right hand column, lines 3-4.  A statement showing the\ndetermination of the Termination Payment will be prepared.  It\'s unclear\nwhether the City is entitled to review and challenge the determination\nbefore a dispute is referred to arbitration.  The City should be entitled to\nreceive a copy of the determination and to question it before it is\nobligated to pay the Termination Payment.  Please clarify, or permit the\nCity to exercise these rights.\n\n7.  Section 4.2(iv) specifies that a Triggering Event will exist if a\nbankruptcy petition is undismissed within 30 days.  Is this (under\nbankruptcy laws) the minimum period of time within which one may seek\ndismissal of a bankruptcy petition?  Please refer to the 11 USC section that\nbacks up this provision, or change to 60 days.\n\n8.  Section 4.2(v) and (vi):  Please change "30 days" to "5 days."  The City\nis concerned with the number of days that Enron may be permitted to fail to\nSchedule before a Triggering Event is triggered by Enron.\n\n9.  Section 4.2(ix):  this language discusses a default by Enron Corp.\n(ENA\'s parent?), but no mention is made of ENA\'s default in this regard?\nPlease explain.\n\n10. Section 4.5, line 4:  Is "a Company" supposed to refer to "the Company"\n?\n\n11. Article 5.  The City is uncomfortable with the force majeure provision\nas drafted.  It states that the parties must perform even if a FM event\n(earthquake) would prevent either or both parties from performing with the\n60-day period stated therein.  There is no such limitation under California\nlaw in the absence of a contract provision to the contrary.\n\n12.  Article 7, Section 7.2:  Could Enron translate the last sentence?  We\ndon\'t understand it.\n\n13.  Appendix "1":  Act:  Please explain why Section 3 is referred to?\n\n14.  Appendix "1", Claims, line 4:  Please add "reasonable" before\n"attorneys\' fees.\n\n 15.  Appendix "1", GAAP:  This should read: "GAAP means generally accepted\naccounting principles, consistently applied, with respect to Company, and\ngovernmental generally accepted accounting principles, consistently applied,\nwith respect to Customer."\n\n16.  Appendix "1", Interest Rate:  Please delete "two percent over".  The\nCity has a AAA bond rating, therefore, the  City believes the 2% over prime\nshould not apply to it.\n\n17.  Appendix "1", Material Adverse Change:  What does Enron believe the\nCity\'s Net Worth to be?  The $400 million threshold is mentioned.  Also,\nwhat is ENA\'s bond rating?  Is "BBB-" an investment grade rating?\n\n18.  Representations and Warranties:  Because we have agreed that the\nopinion of counsel will not be required, the reps and warranties are being\ndeleted.  But the "Representations and Warranties" is nevertheless included\nin the agreement.  Item (i) should be deleted, because the City has not\nundertaken a court search as is our custom and practice whenever we issue an\nopinion.  We would like to delete "and (vii) it is not ... Party."\n\n19.  Operational Flow Orders, line 8:  Please add "reasonable" before\n"attorneys\' fees."\n\n20.  Financial Matters, line 8:  What is meant by "to the extent it has a\nlegal right of access thereto and/or ...etc."\n\n21.  Arbitration, Disputes to be Arbitrated.  We do not as a matter of legal\npolicy agree to arbitration, but we will mediate disputes.  Is Enron\namenable to mediation?  This process is less formal and less costly in my\nopinion.\n\n22.  Authority for Transactions.  Staff would like the Agreement to include\na list of employees for Company and Customer who are authorized to trade on\nbehalf of their employers.  Could a statement be added to this section to\nthis effect?  Then, we could attach the list(s) as an Exhibit C.\n\nThank you so much for considering these issues.  There are others which I\nhope to receive from staff next week and which I will forward to you for\nresponse.\n\nLook forward to hearing from you soon.  I will be out of town after today\nuntil Wednesday, March 7.\n\nSincerely,\n\nGrant Kolling\n  -----Original Message-----\n  From: Dan.J.Hyvl@enron.com [mailto:Dan.J.Hyvl@enron.com]\n  Sent: Tuesday, February 27, 2001 6:16 AM\n  To: grant_kolling@city.palo-alto.ca.us\n  Cc: Kim.Ward@enron.com\n  Subject: Re:  Enfolio Master Firm Purchase/Sale\nAgreement\n\n   << File: 2001-002ctr.doc >>\n  (See attached file: 2001-002ctr.doc)\n\n  Grant,\n       I have incorporated the language you provided to me in\nthe attached\n  document.  I have been informed by the Corporate Secretary\'s\noffice that\n  they will issue a Certificate of Incumbency showing that the\nperson\n  executing the contract for ENA is authorized to execute\ncontracts for ENA.\n  No other party signs as to form or terms, however, the\nofficer executing\n  for ENA will require that the deal person and I initial on\nthe line next to\n  his signature.  I have reviewed the proposed draft\nresolution.  ENA will\n  accept the enacted resolution and will not require that the\nCity Attorney\n  issue an opinion.  If the attached contract is acceptable,\nplease print off\n  2 originals, have them approved, signed and forward to me\nfor ENA\'s\n  approval and signature.  Once the contract is fully\nexecuted, I will return\n  one fully executed original to you for the City\'s file.\n\n - 0071988 RESO Enron.doc\n'}

Marie sends an email to Todd Perkins, attaching draft ISDA Master Agreements for review. Veronica provides comments on the ISDA agreements, highlighting changes for each company. Marie then forwards Todd's comments on the ISDA schedules to Veronica. Todd confirms receiving the email and asks if he should send his comments back to Marie. Marie responds, saying she will direct the comments to the appropriate individuals.

Marie asks Tanya to find copies of the guaranties for Coral Energy. Tanya provides a breakdown of the activity to be included in the Coral Master Netting, including physical power and gas trading with various entities. Marie also mentions a missing power master with Coral Power LLC. Sharon confirms the contracts ECC has with Coral Energy Canada, Inc. Peter asks Sharon to confirm the contracts ECPC has with Coral Energy Canada, Inc.

There is a correction regarding the receipt point for offer #30496, which is Broad Run, not Leach. Chris Germany asks Michael Garred to confirm the top 4 contracts. Michael Garred points out that one contract should already be in ENA's name. Chris Germany confirms that the top 3 contracts were released to CES and the bottom one to ENA. Michael Garred asks Jeff Porter to verify the mdq's in yellow and if they need to take the Gulf capacity per the LDC. Chris Germany informs Michael Garred that Jeff is now on the network and cannot receive emails sent to his old address.

The email thread consists of multiple forwards of a cat video clip from Heidi Jo Warnick to David Kaiser, who then forwards it to Jared Kaiser. The subject of the email is "cat clip." The purpose of the email is to cheer up David Kaiser after a long day of work. The video clip is titled "SCCat.MPG." Jared Kaiser forwards the email to John Craig Taylor, Andrea Ring, and Susan W Pereira, hoping to spread some cheer.

Rob Cass is requesting Tana Jones' assistance in preparing termination letters for four EnronOnline transactions that were made in error. The transactions involved Coral Energy Holding L.P. and Morgan Stanley Capital Group, Inc. Due to an inadvertent entry in the EnronOnline production system, the transactions were not reflective of normal pricing. All parties agreed to terminate the transactions without confirmation. No confirmations were generated, and termination letters may be required by Legal. Bob Bowen provides the specific details of the trades, and Tana asks for the deal particulars to prepare the terminations.

Michael Neves has been consistently sending emails to Tana Jones, urging her to use the 'Financial Trading Agreements' database on Lotus Notes. He requests her to encourage the Credit team to access the database for master swap agreement status. Neves also offers to provide edit access to team members who don't have it. He forwards the link multiple times and suggests that Fred's group should explore the database's usefulness.

Carol St. Clair asks Tana Jones to provide the password for accessing ISDA Opinions on the website. Tana informs Carol that Mark Haedicke couldn't find the password, so she needs to call ISDA. Carol also mentions that EES wants access to the website using their password. Holly Keiser asks Tana if she was able to locate the password, to which Tana responds that Mark Haedicke should have it and will find it when he returns to the office. Carol initially requested the password because Mark was ill and might not be able to look into it before the deadline.

Mike is requesting to rank a new employee from Broadband high enough to keep him. Jeanie asks if he came from another rotation in trading. Mike then asks to place Elizabeth Shim at 60 or below because she is under a performance review plan. He also mentions a new employee, Zack McCarroll, and asks if he needs to be added to the list. Jeanie confirms that Elizabeth Shim was not on the list. Patti asks if it is possible to keep Liz in the weekend rotation to help Shannon out. Mike informs Patti that Elizabeth Shim will be moving into an analyst role in two weeks and asks her to focus on the project until then.

Bob will not be attending the Questar Southern Trails data room because he will be on vacation. Mark confirms that the team will be attending the data room on Monday and Tuesday. He provides details about the location, contacts, and availability of staff for interviews. Mark also mentions that some attendees are staying at the Salt Lake City Marriott. Steve informs Mark that he will only be attending on Tuesday.

The sender is unsure of their plans and will email tomorrow with an update. The recipient suggests a phone call on Saturday morning. Another person mentions a plan to go down early and drink beers at the peacock.

There is also a mention of the Sunday Video Briefing, which can be found on the Research and Gas Fundamentals web pages.

There is a new or modified message in the EOL Terminations mail file. The London Fax System has received multiple faxes, and there are concerns about the system. The sender is unsure if there is a similar system in North America and if they are expected to review all the faxes. They also want to know if there is a way to filter out junk faxes and who to address their questions to.

An email was sent to all Enron employees inviting them to an all-employee meeting on October 23. The meeting will review third quarter financial and operating highlights and discuss action steps based on survey results. Employees who cannot attend in person can access the meeting via streaming video/audio or video teleconferencing. There is also an option to join via telephone. The email also mentions that Steve's 2002 Plan meeting will need to be rescheduled.

Kate Symes emails multiple recipients to request assistance in adding a new counterparty name, Sierra Pacific Holding Company, to Enpower. Kate later confirms that the name has been entered into the system. Rhonda Denton asks if anyone has responded to Kate's request. Cheryl Johnson informs Kate that counterparty requests should be directed to the Global Counterparty group, specifically Sam Schott. Willie Harrell forwards Kate's request to Sam Schott and provides his contact information for further assistance.

Tony has not returned yet, but he is still trying to secure Harper gas. Richard is unsure why it is taking so long, but suspects it is due to the people Tony deals with. There are potential opportunities for PGL to buy Vent and sell Harper, but dealing with PGL is slower than dealing with Tony. Geoff is wondering if he should forget about the gas or if Tony is still working on it. Richard mentions that Tony has an offer from Husky at Ventura plus 0.03, but he is still looking for better offers.

This really puts CA and the ISO on notice that \nthey cannot confiscate the power as they seem ready to do -- FERC reiterates \nthat the generators can sell power wherever they want because the cap is a \ncap on ISO purchases.  ANd if the ISO want to set a sale price cap it has to \nfile with FERC, wait 60 days and amend its contract\n---------------------- Forwarded by Susan J Mara/SFO/EES on 08/01/2000 01:01 \nAM ---------------------------\n\n\n"Daniel Douglass" <douglass@ArterHadden.com> on 07/31/2000 07:27:24 PM\nTo: <peter.bray@att.net>, <JBarthrop@electric.com>, <mnelson@electric.com>, \n<rschlanert@electric.com>, <Bruno_Gaillard@enron.com>, <kmagrude@enron.com>, \n<mpetroch@enron.com>, <susan_j_mara@enron.com>, <athomas@newenergy.com>, \n<bchen@newenergy.com>, <Jeff.Hanson@phaser.com>, <anchau@shellus.com>, \n<andrew.madden@utility.com>, <ben.reyes@utility.com>, \n<chris.king@utility.com>, <david.bayless@utility.com>\ncc:  \nSubject: FERC Order on Morgan Stanley Complaint Against ISO\n\n\nWe have good news on the ISO price caps front.  The FERC has made it\nclear that ISO does not have the ability to mandate that generators sell to \nISO at its price caps and that the proper response to inadequate supply is to \nlift the price caps.\n\nOn Friday, the FERC issued its Order on Complaint in connection with the July \n10 complaint filed by Morgan Stanley Capital Group Inc. ("MS").  As you may \nrecall, MS requested FERC to issue a stay of the ISO\'s maximum purchase price \nauthority and to direct the ISO to reverse any price cap reductions.  MS \nsought Fast Track processing pursuant to Rule 206(h), which was granted by \nFERC on the grounds that the complaint "warrants expeditious action."\n\nAs a quick background summary for you, last November, FERC issued an order \napproving Tariff Amendment 21 which extended ISO\'s price cap authority \nthrough 11/15/00.  That order stated that the ISO "maximum purchase price was \nnot a cap on what the seller may charge the ISO, but a cap on what the ISO \nwas willing to pay."  The Commission said that sellers dissatisfied with the \nprice cap could "choose to sell those services into the California Power \nExchange or bilateral markets."\n\nFERC notes in Friday\'s Order that the 6/28 the ISO\'s Board resolution lowered \nthe caps to $500 and ISO further directed that, "To the extent permitted by \nlaw, regulation and pre-existing contract, Management shall direct generators \nto bid in all their capacity when system load exceeds 38,000 MW."\n\nThe MS complaint alleged that the cap reduction was unlawful and would, \n"threaten the stability and integroty of the marketplace."  MS also requested \nan emergency technical conference to examine ISO\'s justification for the \nprice cap reduction.\n\nFERC denied the MS stay request, as well as its request that the $750 maximum \npurchase price be reinstated.  The Commission reiterates that it is not \napproving a cap on sellers\' prices, because they can sell at whatever price \nthey want.  Rather ISO has simply stated the maximum price it is willing to \npay.  "Because sellers are not required to sell to the ISO, the ISO cannot \ndictate their price."\n\nImportantly, however, FERC also states that, "ISO has no more or less ability \nto procure capacity and energy than any other buyer of these services....if \nthe ISO is unable to elicit sufficient supplies at or below its announced \npurchase price ceiling (because generators are free to sell elsewhere if they \nchoose), it will have to raise its purchase price to the level necessary to \nmeet its needs."  [Emphasis added]  FERC then notes that this may lead to an \nincrease in Out of Market ("OOM") calls and that OOM calls are not subject to \na maximum purchase price.\n\nAlso, with regard to the ISO\'s resolution stating that generators must bid \ntheir capacity into the ISO markets when system load exceeds 38,000 MW, FERC \nstates clearly that, "such a requirement is not permitted by our November  12 \nOrder and the ISO tariff."  [Emphasis added]\n\nFERC goes on to say that any requirement to sell to ISO in conjunction with a \nmaximum purchase price would require significant revisions to ISO\'s market \nrules, which could not be made effective without a corresponding amendment to \nISO\'s tariff.  This would require 60 days\' advance notice, "and could not be \nimplemented prior to Commission approval.  As stated above, our November 12 \nOrder was clearly based on the premise that the proper response to inadequate \nsupply (due to a low maximum purchase price) is to raise the maximum purchase \nprice."\n\nISO is then "put on notice that any amendment to mandate sales must be \naccompanied by a demonstration that this extreme measure is the proper \nresponse to low supplies in the ISO markets."\n\nConcurrences were filed by Commissioners Massey and Hebert.  Massey suggests \nthat the state has to facilitate solutions to market issues, such as risk \nmanagement tools, removing constraints on hedging opportunities, introducing \nreal time pricing through real time metering and expediting approval of new \ngeneration and transmission projects in California.  Hebert says that the \nprevious November Order tried to "straddle the fence" and that, "Today, the \nCommission at least starts to lean slightly in the right direction of \nrecognizing that we have a role."  He then reiterates his preference for \nremoving all price caps.  He also suggests that, "Getting to the bottom of \nthe problem, in my view, requires us to begin a proceeding to rescind our \napproval of the ISO as operator of the California grid.  The record supports \nsuch a move."  He refers approvingly to the Collins resignation letter, \nstating that it, "thoughtfully outlines consequences to the market of a \nreturn to \'command and control.\' "  Hebert states that, "The independence of \nthe ISO\'s governing structure stands threatened. This is an important development and very good news in our ongoing \nefforts to seek economic sanity at the ISO.\n\nPlease call if you have any questions.\n\nDan\n'}

("MS").  As you may \nrecall, MS requested FERC to issue a stay of the ISO\'s maximum purchase price \nauthority and to direct the ISO to reverse any price cap reductions.  MS \nsought Fast Track processing pursuant to Rule 206(h), which was granted by \nFERC on the grounds that the complaint "warrants expeditious action."\n\nAs a quick background summary for you, last November, FERC issued an order \napproving Tariff Amendment 21 which extended ISO\'s price cap authority \nthrough 11/15/00.  That order stated that the ISO "maximum purchase price was \nnot a cap on what the seller may charge the ISO, but a cap on what the ISO \nwas willing to pay."  The Commission said that sellers dissatisfied with the \nprice cap could "choose to sell those services into the California Power \nExchange or bilateral markets."\n\nFERC notes in Friday\'s Order that the 6/28 the ISO\'s Board resolution lowered \nthe caps to $500 and ISO further directed that, "To the extent permitted by \nlaw, regulation and pre-existing contract, Management shall direct generators \nto bid in all their capacity when system load exceeds 38,000 MW."\n\nThe MS complaint alleged that the cap reduction was unlawful and would, \n"threaten the stability and integroty of the marketplace." Rather ISO has simply stated the maximum price it is willing to \npay.  "Because sellers are not required to sell to the ISO, the ISO cannot \ndictate their price."\n\nImportantly, however, FERC also states that, "ISO has no more or less ability \nto procure capacity and energy than any other buyer of these services....if \nthe ISO is unable to elicit sufficient supplies at or below its announced \npurchase price ceiling (because generators are free to sell elsewhere if they \nchoose), it will have to raise its purchase price to the level necessary to \nmeet its needs." Hebert says that the \nprevious November Order tried to "straddle the fence" and that, "Today, the \nCommission at least starts to lean slightly in the right direction of \nrecognizing that we have a role."  He then reiterates his preference for \nremoving all price caps.  He also suggests that, "Getting to the bottom of \nthe problem, in my view, requires us to begin a proceeding to rescind our \napproval of the ISO as operator of the California grid.  The record supports \nsuch a move."  He refers approvingly to the Collins resignation letter, \nstating that it, "thoughtfully outlines consequences to the market of a \nreturn to \'command and control.\' "  Hebert states that, "The independence of \nthe ISO\'s governing structure stands threatened.  We should \'stand up,\' to \nquote the resignation letter."  Hebert advocates opening a section 206 \nproceeding now, as part of the recently announced inquiry into bulk power \nmarkets, "including the California markets."\n\nThis decision makes it clear that ISO cannot lower the caps at tomorrow\'s \nmeeting and expect that sellers will be required to sell to it at that \nprice.  This is an important development and very good news in our ongoing \nefforts to seek economic sanity at the ISO.\n\nPlease call if you have any questions.\n\nDan\n\n\n'}

summary: The FERC has issued an order in response to a complaint filed by Morgan Stanley, stating that the ISO cannot mandate that generators sell to ISO at its price caps. The FERC reiterates that generators can sell power wherever they want because the cap is a cap on ISO purchases. If the ISO wants to set a sale price cap, it has to file with FERC, wait 60 days, and amend its contract. Commissioners Massey and Hebert concur with the order and suggest various solutions to market issues. This decision is seen as a positive development in seeking economic sanity at the ISO.

summary: The email thread discusses the testing methods used by SGS at loadport and discharge in Thailand and the Philippines. Britt Davis requests clarification on whether SGS tested using both ASTM D3605 without ashing and with ashing, and if the results were consistent. Janice Moore suggests conducting joint testing using the same method used at loadport for consistency. Matt Lee mentions the importance of metals testing and proposes using "ashing" for the joint testing to avoid conflict with existing loadport sample results. The preference for US experts over European experts is also mentioned.

Nicole has sent a revised version of the Guarantee with proposed changes and a note indicating the changes made to the original form. She will confirm the provisions of Section 8 with Derek Halvorsen at BP. She asks Nicole to review the events in the preamble and provide any comments. Tanya suggests setting up a meeting with Hodge and Penman to discuss the situation. Molly sends a proposed guarantee to Nicor to cover enovate exposure and asks for comments. Jeff Hodge's letter is attached.

Melissa informs Phillip that she has a dentist appointment at 9:30 am and will be gone for about 45 minutes. Rain also mentions having a dentist appointment at 12:30 pm during their lunch hour and expects to be back in one hour. The last two emails seem to be mistakenly sent and contain incomplete information about a dentist appointment on January 25th at 7:45 am and sending an email to Ed.

Stephanie Panus informs Sara Shackleton that Thay Bishop sent the agreement back to them in November, but they are currently trying to locate a copy to send to them. Sara asks Stephanie to call Ty regarding the termination notice, as it relates to the ISDA, which they do not have. Stephanie confirms that they have not received the executed ISDA from MARTA.

Kay is requesting a Connecticut lawyer to review a contract draft for the purchase of Fuel Cell equipment. She is concerned about the request for a security interest in the equipment and wants to verify the lien rights under Connecticut law. John is asked to provide a fatal flaw analysis or recommend Connecticut counsel. Another email discusses the need to resolve outstanding business issues with FuelCells and the importance of finalizing the technical aspects of the purchase order. The email also mentions the need for revised cost estimates and a state filing. Marion expresses interest in discussing Fuel Cell technology and asks for a copy of the purchase order form. Scott mentions the need for a development agreement and construction MOU.

TD Waterhouse sent multiple emails to gstorey@enron.com regarding trade confirmations for their account. The emails provide a link to view the trade confirmation online and instructions to verify the accuracy of the information. They also mention the option to update delivery preferences and provide contact information for any discrepancies. The emails emphasize the importance of not sending sensitive information via email.

Lisa is following up on the status of the risk books for December. She wants to know if the books are final and if there are any updates on the categories of deals, such as legally terminated, not performing but not terminated, and still performing. She mentions that the deals that are still performing should have liquidations as normal, while the remainder will be frozen until an amount is settled with the counterparty. Lisa is trying to get as much done before splitting with the people going to NETCO. Kam provides the official post-IDs from December 31st for all live deals, including those in the bankruptcy book. Jeffrey asks Kam to provide a list of the final post-IDs for the estate, bankruptcy, and performing post-IDs for gas and power.

Kelly will be a power trader at Duke, but it is unclear if she has experience in that role. The weather group left, possibly due to dissatisfaction with lateral moves and rejected offers. The sender is considering applying at UBS, as they are hiring weather professionals. They also mention trying to contact Scott Neal. The sender asks for Kam's updated address to send a wedding invite. Kam suggests looking into Duke for job opportunities and mentions that they are hiring Enron employees.

The email thread discusses a summary of FERC's 12-15 order on California Markets. Mary Hain forwards the summary to Alan Comnes, expressing gratitude for a Christmas gift. The summary is attached to the email. The email is also forwarded to a large group of recipients, including Enron employees and external contacts.

The email thread discusses a proposed solution for the financial issues faced by PG&E. The solution involves a government entity becoming an ESP and taking over all customers not served by another ESP. The government entity would charge the frozen rate plus 10% until the end of 2002 and assure all ESPs that their costs will not exceed 110% of the frozen rate. The rate freeze and surcharge would continue until the end of March 2002. The government would also commit to building 10,000 MW of generation and allowing emission-constrained generators to buy emission credits.

Chairman Hoecker has proposed a list of questions to Enron regarding the Nov. 1 meeting. The responses are due on Wednesday the 22nd. Susan Mara expresses concern that Hoecker may have received the questions from Rozja or the CPUC. Ron Carroll at Bracewell will work with the CPUC subpoena group to address the questions. Mary Hain asks if responses are being drafted and suggests keeping them in line with the larger response. Lysa Akin forwards the questions to the EES group, and Nancy Pickover attaches the list of questions.

Mike Driscol from Prebon provided prices for a deal where Enron sells 25 mw of Q2'02 NP-15 peak hours from Sempra. The initial price was $98.00, but it was later changed to $97.95 for one deal and $98 for another. However, Mike couldn't confirm the prices that evening, so they planned to check in the morning. Evelyn Metoyer asked for an update on the status of these prices.

There is a reorientation session scheduled for Wednesday, March 27th from 9:00-10:30am in EB5C2. Kevin Hyatt suggests that any other day is fine, while Teb Lokey requests a reschedule for another day as March 20th is full. Kevin Hyatt also cancels his attendance for the session on March 7th due to a conflict. Michelle Lokay and Lindy Donoho confirm their attendance for the sessions on March 5th and 7th respectively.

Kam asks Russ to remap the Koch/Zone 2 Area 5/004708 meter to GDP-Colgulf/LA and IF-Colgulf/LA. Susan confirms that Alejandra is calculating Gulf 2. George mentions that they will remap after NE Gulf 2 is calculated and asks if Susan is the one who calculates Gulf 2. Kam asks Russ to remap KOCH/Zone 4 Area 3/000464 to IF-Tetco/ELA and GDP-Tetco/ELA. Kam also mentions that the fix will take effect overnight and Susan will see the impact in tomorrow's P&L.

Jesus Melendrez has requested the termination of several swaps that are not profitable for ENA. Nancy has organized folders for each swap and Eric Boyt has been asked to provide updated values. Mary is concerned about the involvement of Nora Dobin and the potential impact on volumetric production payment vehicles. Kay identifies one of the swaps as belonging to Sara. Nancy suggests involving a swap attorney familiar with ISDAs and ENA's current position. The main question is what approval is needed to terminate the swaps. The relevant swaps are Cresendo Energy LLC, Juniper, CGAS, and East Sour Lake.

There are several email threads discussing happy hour plans. One thread is about a happy hour at King Biscuit in Houston Heights on January 30th at 6:00pm. Another thread is about a happy hour at the Front Porch on West Gray on November 29th at 5:30pm. There is also a discussion about a happy hour at Ruggles Enron - Dynegy Field. In another thread, there is a suggestion for a happy hour at Kenneally's at 5:00pm. Lastly, there is a happy hour planned at Little Woodrow's downtown on October 25th at 5:00pm to bid farewell to a colleague.

The email thread consists of a conversation between Landry and Lenhart. Lenhart apologizes for leaving abruptly and explains that he went to get pizza and passed out due to the shots he had with some girls. Landry asks about Lenhart's whereabouts at CAT's. They discuss the declining stock of Enron and the possibility of issuing more stock, which could cause the stock to drop to $10. Landry also mentions a forwarded article about Enron's financial situation.

Terrie James is planning the agenda for the Management Conference and wants to include a panel to provide an overview of each primary operating unit. Louise Kitchen expresses dissatisfaction with the panel format from the previous year and hopes for a major change. Terrie explains that the purpose of the panel is to highlight the operations of the business and showcase the next level of leadership. Mark Frevert will moderate the panel, introducing each participant and generating discussion. The panel is scheduled for November 16, and presentations should be no more than 10 minutes.

Because of the interactive nature of  these sessions the class size must be limited. Ideally, we would prefer no more  than two participants from each company. Please select the individual(s) from  your company who will attend these sessions, and forward the attached  registration brochure to them.   Please advise me if your needs exceed the requested attendance guideline  of two people per company. We will make every effort to accommodate your  request.\nWe recognize that asking you to sustain a  steady commitment of time, resources and manpower is an exacting demand.  Your confidence that your Market Trials  participants gain as much knowledge about the Midwest ISO's operational  abilities is equally important to us.\nWe are grateful for your continued support  of the Midwest ISO and look forward to working with you during the Market Trials  period. \n \nSincerely,\n [IMAGE]\nJames  . Torgerson\nPresident and  CEO\nThe Midwest  ISO\n \ncc:  Advisory Committee, MISO Market Trials  contacts\n\n - orientation registration 3.pdf << File: orientation registration 3.pdf >> \n - clip_image002.jpg << File: clip_image002.jpg >> "}]"}
summary: The Midwest ISO has sent a letter to transmission owners, expressing gratitude for their support and providing information about the upcoming Market Trials period. They are offering two types of orientation sessions to facilitate participation: one on the Electronic Scheduling Process and another on overall Market Trials Orientation. The sessions are interactive and have limited class sizes. The ISO requests no more than two participants per company. Attendees are encouraged to identify gaps between current operations and the new market. The ISO appreciates the commitment and looks forward to working together.

The email thread discusses the payment terms for three contract types agreed upon at a management team meeting. Keith Harris explains that the error correction mechanism protects both AssetCo and EngCo from being ripped off, but it can blunt incentives if the trigger point for error correction is too close to the target cost. Libby Gawith raises concerns about the proposal, stating that it is at odds with industry norms and that EngCo would be taking on too much risk. Keith agrees that more work is needed in this area and suggests setting up a sub-group to work through the details.

John is unable to attend the New Year's Kickoff Reception on January 11 because he will be out of the country. Kim has added it to his schedule in case his plans change. Vince Kaminski confirms his attendance. Cathy P. asks if this reception is different from the one on Mike McConnell's calendar for January 16, as he will be at an off-site meeting on the 11th.

Louise is requesting Vince to call her regarding a transfer that needs to be facilitated before he leaves. She emphasizes that they have been asking for this for weeks and asks Mark to help resolve the issue. Vince reminds everyone that the members of the Research Group who stayed behind will be leaving in a week, so they need to accelerate the process. Jim asks if the state has copies of all programs and suggests that systems should manage the migration. He also mentions that Muller was supposed to send Vince the contract indicating the section requiring the turnover.

Chris Germany contacted Janelle Shaunghnessy at CMS Marketing to inquire about the payment for their March 2002 production invoice. The invoice was for the sale of 50,000 dth per day of Michcon Storage gas, totaling $3,695,975. Janelle confirmed that she had not received the invoice yet, so Chris faxed it to her. Janelle stated that they should be able to make the payment the following day. Chris later confirmed that Janelle received the faxed invoice. Priscilla Hamic mentioned that the invoice had been faxed multiple times.

Karen asks her colleagues to confirm their attendance for lunch and requests two people for an office visit. Jason declines lunch due to a busy week and covering for someone on vacation. Debra offers to run interference between Richard and someone else, but Karen clarifies that she was asking for their interests, not hers.

The final plans for Jason's bachelor party have been made. The group will meet at Cinemark Theaters on Richmond and Sam Houston Parkway at 5 pm sharp. From there, they will head to a cruise in Freeport, departing at 7 pm on January 19th. The cost will be $32 per person, which Eric has already paid. Unfortunately, the gourmet dinner option is not available, so they will have to settle for a buffet dinner. Transportation will be arranged, and Eric will provide further details in a future email.

John recommends a candidate from EBS who previously worked for Marcello Romano and traded oil products at Goldman. He suggests getting Louise's opinion. Sally asks for a resume and a meeting. Paula recommends Norma Tidrow from Azurix, praising her work and skills. Rick supports the candidate but expresses concern about their reluctance to move. Stinson forwards the resume of Samer's friend from Azurix to Vince. Chonawee inquires about a position in Enron Research Group and sends their resume and transcript. Hector recommends his friend for the Research Group.

The email thread discusses a new EOL product called the Day Ahead/Real-Time Park/Lend product. It is a financial trade settled in real-time on a day-ahead basis. The product allows parties to take positions in real-time, even if they are not a control area, and provides utilities and generators the ability to hedge a day-ahead position. The thread includes discussions about contract language and mechanics for the product. Kevin is identified as the person to talk to about the product.

John has sent an email to Charlie, with Mark copied, regarding gas swap pricing for two deals: NICOR and Anadarko (Carthage). John has attached two files with notes to clarify the request, and mentions that a notional price is acceptable for now. It is unclear if Charlie is aware of these deals, as John asks if he has any questions. Mark has asked John to forward the email to Charlie.

Mark Greenberg, Senior Counsel at Enron, has sent multiple emails to various individuals regarding the review and signing of agreements. He attaches the BETA Agreement and Fee Agreement for the BrokerClient products and requests that they be reviewed and signed if acceptable. He provides clean versions of the agreements as well. He mentions that there were previous discussions and changes made to the agreements. He also mentions that there may be additional changes proposed by Bob or Michael. He asks for the documents to be printed, signed, and forwarded for countersignature. He thanks the recipients for their cooperation.

Carol North works in the Credit Group and will be working with Aparna Rajaram and Ken Curry. Tana Jones wants to ensure that she only receives ClickPaper approvals from the Credit Group. Walter Guidroz confirms that Carol North is part of the Credit Group and should be added to any ClickPaper distribution lists. The discussion clarifies the roles of different individuals in supporting credit for Enron Industrial Markets and Enron Global Markets.

The email thread consists of multiple unrelated messages. The first email asks for the titles of several individuals at UBS Warburg Energy. The second email is an insulting message to an Enron spokesperson. The third email is a recommendation for a tailor. The fourth email asks about the mechanics of OFOs and the treatment of imbalances. The summary captures the main points of each email, including the requests and questions posed by the senders.

The email thread discusses the development of fundamental operating standards and controls in the Wholesale Services group. The goal is to have effective exception reporting on critical standards by the end of the year. The exception report will be used as a tool to allocate resources and address any issues. The thread also mentions the need for diagnostic measures to assess adherence to the standards, such as accurate and timely recording of transactions and daily management P&L reporting. The importance of involving all operating companies in the design of the reports is emphasized.

Frank is excited about being selected for a second round interview at Enron and looks forward to meeting Vince and the research group. Van declines Enron's offer and will be working at Salomon Smith Barney in New York. Vince asks Carlos for the phone numbers of two individuals and Carlos provides the numbers. Vince asks Carlos to forward their resumes for an interview. Carlos agrees and mentions a possible postdoctoral/trainee agreement. Vince asks Carlos for the resumes again. Carlos provides the resumes and discusses a visit. Stinson informs Carlos that Vince is interested in meeting and collaborating. Vince confirms his availability to speak at a conference in Toronto. Phelim apologizes for missing Vince's call and provides his contact information. Mark thanks Anita for her contribution to the Singapore office.

The email thread consists of a conversation between two friends, Kim and Laura. Kim reaches out to Laura to check on her and discuss potential plans for a girls' weekend in Chicago. Laura expresses her excitement about the idea and mentions her husband's travel schedule. Kim also mentions her relationship with Pete and her desire for Laura to visit Houston. They both express their well wishes for each other and look forward to meeting up soon.

Debra Perlingiere forwarded an email thread to Stacey Richardson regarding the confirmation of certain deals. Stacey was only able to print the confirm for one deal, which was split into two due to being a two-month firm deal. Stacey couldn't find the other deals in the system and suggested contacting the Confirms group for assistance. Cheryl Dudley offered help with HPL contracts and deals. Debra apologized for involving Stacey and mentioned that the HPL group had already indicated they didn't have the documents.

Edmund has made some amendments to the proposed GTCs and has requested that Gavin prepare amended versions. Mark has some questions and minor points about the GTCs, including the use of executed confirmation as controlling evidence, the treatment of online credit derivatives under existing master agreements, the fraud limitation in Section 6, the authority to amend the ETA, the definition of Bankruptcy Event, the use of the term "Month," the interest rate for non-US$ payments, the inclusion of arbitration language, and the absence of confidentiality provisions. Edmund responds to Mark's points and makes additional changes to Section 11(D).

The email thread consists of a conversation between Patrice and Ora about meeting up at 5:00 PM. Patrice initially asks if Ora is "rolling," to which Ora responds with a playful reminder to say "same bat place, same bat time." Patrice then confirms the meeting time and place, and Ora mentions that she arrived at work early and left late the previous night. The conversation repeats with the same content multiple times.

Steve Westlund confirms that he and his wife Julie will be playing golf on Sunday. However, he discovers that there is no tee time reserved for Stan Horton at Raveneaux Country Club. As a backup, Steve reserves a tee time at 9:45 am on the New Course. He advises Stan to double check with the Pro Shop. Cindy, Stan's assistant, contacts the Pro Shop and confirms that the tee time for Stan and his group is indeed at 8:15 am on the Old Course. Chris Gann also confirms his attendance.

There is an email thread with multiple forwards containing a file named "AHMED.MPEG." The original sender, Donny Cox, warns against taking someone hunting, but the content of the file is unknown. The email has been forwarded by Kevin Jolly to Rufino Doroteo and Dana Davis. The thread consists of multiple duplicates of the same email, with no additional information or discussion provided.
